bib.title: Vector Search with OpenAI Embeddings: Lucene Is All You Need

question: Is a dedicated vector store necessary for dense retrieval, or can Lucene HNSW indexes with an off-the-shelf embedding API do the job?
hypothesis: Lucene's HNSW indexes are adequate for bi-encoder vector search, so the cost of a separate vector store is not justified by its benefits.
contributions: A reproducible end-to-end demonstration of vector search with OpenAI ada2 embeddings indexed in Lucene (Anserini) on MS MARCO passage ranking
A cost-benefit argument against dedicated vector stores for brownfield search deployments
Release of the OpenAI embeddings for the MS MARCO corpus

method.summary: Encoded all MS MARCO v1 passages and queries with OpenAI ada2 embeddings via API, indexed the vectors with Lucene 9.5.0 HNSW through Anserini (with a patch to lift the 1024-dim limit), and evaluated retrieval effectiveness and throughput.
method.task: passage retrieval (dense bi-encoder, MS MARCO passage ranking)

datasets.name: MS MARCO passage corpus
datasets.split: corpus; queries: dev, TREC DL19, TREC DL20
datasets.preprocessing: passages truncated to 512 tokens; average 75.2 tiktoken tokens per passage, approx. 660 million tokens total

inference.samples: throughput averaged over four separate trials after a warmup run, on MS MARCO dev queries
inference.retrieval: Lucene 9.5.0 HNSW via Anserini; M=16, efC=100, no final segment optimization; efSearch=1000; 1000 hits per query; dot-product scoring

other.encoding_time: two days for corpus and queries
other.hardware: two Intel Xeon Platinum 8160 (24 cores each, 2.10 GHz), 1 TB RAM, Ubuntu 18.04, ZFS
other.lucene_workaround: Lucene HNSW capped vectors at 1024 dims; copied Lucene trunk source files into the Anserini tree and patched vector size so local class files override in the fatjar
other.nondeterminism: HNSW indexing is non-deterministic, so effectiveness may vary slightly between runs

eval.protocol: Baseline numbers are Pyserini two-click reproductions (marked *) or copied from original papers; no significance testing; single ada2 run for effectiveness.

availability.data: OpenAI embeddings for MS MARCO freely downloadable (stated)

evidence.quote: Indexing took around three hours with 16 threads, with the parameters M set to 16 and efC set to 100, without final segment optimization.

results.claim: ada2 with Lucene HNSW reaches R@1k of 0.984 on MS MARCO dev, tied with ColBERT-v2 and above the other listed dense models.
results.setup: MS MARCO dev queries, ada2 1536-d embeddings, Lucene 9.5.0 HNSW
results.table: Table 1, row OpenAI ada2, column dev R@1k

results.claim: ada2 RR@10 on MS MARCO dev is 0.343, below SPLADE++ ED (0.383), ColBERT-v2 (0.397) and TCT-ColBERTv2 (0.358), slightly above TAS-B (0.340).
results.setup: MS MARCO dev queries, ada2, Lucene HNSW
results.table: Table 1, row OpenAI ada2, column dev RR@10

results.claim: On DL19 ada2 gets nDCG@10 0.704 and on DL20 0.676.
results.setup: TREC DL19 queries (DL20: 0.676), ada2, Lucene HNSW
results.table: Table 1, row OpenAI ada2, columns DL19 nDCG@10 and DL20 nDCG@10 (0.676)

results.claim: Query throughput of the Lucene HNSW index is 9.8 QPS with 16 threads on a dated high-end server.
results.setup: MS MARCO dev queries, 1000 hits per query, efSearch=1000, 16 threads, 2x Xeon 8160, mean of four trials after warmup
results.quote: we were able to achieve 9.8 queries per second (QPS), fetching 1000 hits per query with the efSearch parameter set to 1000

results.claim: Indexing the corpus took about three hours with 16 threads.
results.setup: M=16, efC=100, 16 threads, no segment optimization, same server
results.quote: Indexing took around three hours with 16 threads

results.claim: Raw 32-bit float vectors would need 54 GB, but the JSON text representation used takes 109 GB gzip-compressed.
results.quote: our collection of vectors takes up 109 GB as compressed text files (using gzip)
results.note: 54 GB is the paper's estimate for raw float32, not measured

results.claim: Corpus is about 660 million tokens, average 75.2 per passage, encoded in two days under a 3500 calls/min rate limit.
results.setup: MS MARCO passages, tiktoken, truncated to 512 tokens
results.quote: we computed the average token count per passage in our corpus to be 75.2, resulting in a total of approximately 660 million tokens

results.claim: Lucene reaches only about half the query throughput of Faiss under comparable settings but scales better with multiple threads.
results.source: Ma, Teofili and Lin 2023 (Anserini Gets Dense Retrieval)
results.setup: Lucene 9.5.0 vs Faiss HNSW, comparable settings
results.quote: Lucene achieves only around half the query throughput of Faiss under comparable settings

results.claim: Authors argue the capability gap between Lucene and dedicated vector stores is mainly performance, not features, so a separate store is not justified for existing Lucene shops.
results.setup: Argument, no head-to-head vector store comparison

results.claim: Authors find pgvector compelling: for an enterprise already on Postgres it adds vector search with minimal extra complexity.

limits: No dedicated vector store (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Qdrant, Chroma) is benchmarked; the claim is a cost-benefit argument, not a measured comparison.
Authors concede Lucene is unequivocally slower than Faiss and lags in indexing speed, latency and throughput.
Required patching Lucene to lift the 1024-dim limit; no release supported 1536 dims as of early August 2023 (dated: later Lucene releases changed this).
Possible MS MARCO leakage into ada2 training is unknown.
Only 9.8 QPS on one dated server; single dataset; HNSW non-determinism means numbers vary slightly; no scale beyond 8.8M passages.
Vespa and pgvector are discussed but not evaluated.
